text:
rachael: Quick heads-up — ACME pilot asked for a 'mid-market hybrid' path: keep our Starter slab but allow a per-route throughput add-on + a premium SLO add-on (on-call pager + 99.9% latency SLA). They want this in contract language and an explicit monthly burst crediting clause. Meeting with their procurement 10:30 PT tomorrow. Can we surface tradeoffs and a recommended path before then?

sam: fyi from sales: ACME will sign if we can guarantee predictable cost for their busiest routes. They expect an escape-hatch that moves traffic to a cheaper model variant if we hit capacity. Also asked for 30% discount if they commit to a 12mo reserved capacity.

kai: technical note: per-route throughput accounting + enforced limits is non-trivial. Router needs per-customer per-route metering + tokenized prioritization. We can approximate with a QoS addon (priority lanes) at the tenancy level but not fine-grained per-route throttles without a few weeks of work.

drew: finance perspective: two asks: (1) burst crediting model — do we net off unused burst against future invoices or do we offer one-time credits? (2) Reserved discount needs a firm commit metric (RPS or token volume). Also need to model revenue leakage if we allow auto-fallback to cheaper model variant.

rachael: proposed options (short):
1) Productized QoS add-on: keep slab tiers unchanged, sell a per-tenant QoS add-on that increases priority and gives X burst tokens per month. Simple to sell, less engineering.
2) Per-route addon (ACME ask): billable per-route capacity buckets + hard limits. High engineering cost, more flexible for customers, higher price.
3) Contract-level fallback: allow automatic routing to a cheaper model variant when thresholds hit; pair with a rebate policy (e.g., 20% token credit for overflow). Lower engineering cost but customer-visible quality regression.

rachael: sample contract language (draft):
```
Customer may purchase Route Capacity Add-Ons ("Route Add-Ons") that allocate dedicated throughput to specific API routes. Route Add-Ons are billed monthly and include a monthly burst allowance. If usage exceeds the allocated throughput and burst, Redwood may, at its discretion, route excess requests to compatible lower-tier model variants. In the event of routing to lower-tier variants, Customer shall be eligible for a pre-defined overflow credit as set forth in the applicable order form.
```

legal-bot: recommended clause tweaks: specify measurement window (UTC month), define "compatible lower-tier model variants" (e.g., same family at a lower performance/quantization tier), and add a 7-day notice for any permanent fallback behavior. Also add data residency callouts if we route cross-region.

kai: engineering estimates: to ship a safe per-route add-on with enforcement + accounting -> 4-6 sprints (core router + billing hook + testing). QoS addon -> 2 sprints. Contract fallback -> feature flagging + routing rules -> 1-2 sprints but needs thorough QA for customer UX.

drew: recommend we offer QoS addon for GA, provide contract fallback as an explicit option in pilot with ACME, and defer per-route add-on to roadmap quarter+1 unless ACME signs a >$1M commit. Need to confirm modeling for revenue crediting.

sam: happy to present that to ACME; they prefer a GA-available product path with a pilot-specific contract appendix. If we position fallback credits responsibly, legal/finance should be fine.

rachael: launch criteria suggestion for pilot (what we commit to ACME):
- QoS addon available in GA (docs + pricing)
- Pilot appendix enabling contract-level fallback for up to 3 named routes, with clear overflow credit formula and max monthly credit cap
- SLO dashboard + alerts configured for ACME routes
- Post-pilot review: decision on building per-route add-on.

rachael: action items before 10:30 PT meeting:
- @kai: one-slide technical tradeoff + rough timeline (by EOD)
- @drew: two pricing scenarios (QoS addon price vs per-route premium + credit policy)
- @legal-bot: draft pilot appendix language with measurement windows + notice terms
- @sam: lead ACME conversation, offer pilot appendix and GA QoS addon as path forward

sam: noted — i'll take the lead. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

rachael: thanks — will consolidate into a 1-pager and drop in the meeting thread.
